summary: Aermotor MC-39 lookout built in 1933 for the Florida Division of Forestry; ownership has reverted to adjacent landowners.

facts.agency: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints

access.note: The register says ownership has reverted to the adjacent landowners. Ask them before going near it.

events.note: Aermotor MC-39 built for the Florida Division of Forestry
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register; nominated by Robert Spear

evidence.supports: built 1933; Aermotor MC-39; 100 to 120 ft; built for Florida Division of Forestry; ownership reverted to adjacent landowners
evidence.quote: This Aermotor MC-39 tower was built in 1933 and is 100 to 120 feet tall. While built for the Florida Division of Forestry, ownership of the tower has reverted to the adjacent landowners.

evidence.supports: administered by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

sources.title: The Aermotor Company: From Windmills to Forest Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: Single-register history: every built, design and registration fact comes from the NHLR page; the Eastern US Lookouts page has no details for Magnolia. The Florida Memory and Lakeland Ledger pages returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text, so they were not read. Who holds the land is unclear: the register says ownership reverted to adjacent landowners and names the LDS church as administrator. Access is marked private on that basis; confirm before publishing. The register gives height only as a 100 to 120 ft range, so no height_m is entered. The record's county, agency and 1933 build year agree with the register.
